identity.what_it_is: The public city beach of Kozhikode (formerly Calicut) on Kerala's Malabar Coast, also marketed as 'Calicut Beach' — a working, historic urban waterfront rather than a resort beach.
identity.where: Western edge of Kozhikode city, Kerala, India, at approx. 11°15'22"N 75°46'10"E; the beach runs roughly from Beypore (south) to Kappad (north) through sections including South Beach, Vellayil, and Kallayi.
identity.warnings: Three distinct nearby beaches are easily conflated with this one in search results and news coverage: (1) Kappad Beach, 16 km north — the actual documented 1498 Vasco da Gama landing site and Kerala's Blue-Flag-certified beach (Feb 2025); Kerala Tourism's own copy for THIS beach implies the Vasco da Gama landing happened here, which is not the historically documented site. (2) Thikkodi Beach, ~25 km north — site of a January 2025 quadruple drowning, a different location. (3) Kothi Beach near Nainamvalappu — where an earlier (Oct 2022) sea-recession event occurred, distinct from the Oct 2025 event at this beach's South Beach. Also, the Wikipedia article titled 'Kuttichira Beach' is actually about an inland historic quarter of Kozhikode, not a real beach — a naming trap, not a near-duplicate coastline.

spike_candidates.statement: Kerala Tourism's page for this beach credits it with Vasco da Gama's 1498 arrival, but the documented landing site is Kappad Beach, 16 km north — the one that actually holds Blue Flag certification.
spike_candidates.tension: A brochure borrows a more famous beach's founding legend and international eco-certification to dress up a beach that has neither.

spike_candidates.statement: On the night of October 15-16, 2025, the sea inexplicably retreated 200 metres along a 1.5 km stretch of the beach, and a near-identical event happened 3 km away in October 2022.
spike_candidates.tension: A recurring, unexplained coastal phenomenon gets a same-day CMFRI site visit and a tidal hand-wave, but no permanent monitoring or public explanation.

spike_candidates.statement: Of Kozhikode district's 53 km of engineered seawalls, a 2022 survey found only 10.5 km still intact and 14.4 km collapsed or in poor condition.
spike_candidates.tension: The postcard image of a paved, lit promenade sits on top of coastal defenses that are, district-wide, more broken than not.

spike_candidates.statement: The same sand that hosted Gandhi, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, Indira Gandhi, and Krishna Menon rallying the independence movement is now sold to visitors mainly as a sunset-and-mussels spot.
spike_candidates.tension: A beach with a real 20th-century political history is marketed almost entirely on scenery, with the politics reduced to a renamed road.

facts.fact: Kozhikode Beach is promoted by Kerala's official tourism board as 'Calicut Beach,' a beach blending scenic, historical, and cultural appeal on the Malabar Coast.
facts.quote: Kozhikode Beach, also known as Calicut Beach, is a tranquil retreat that seamlessly blends scenic beauty, historical significance, and cultural charm.
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach | Calicut Beach | Kerala Coastal Attractions

facts.fact: A separate Wikipedia article titled 'Kuttichira Beach' is not a coastline at all but an inland historic quarter of Kozhikode bounded by the sea, the Kallai river, and Vellayil — a name that misleads anyone assuming it is a nearby swimmable beach.
facts.quote: the Arabian Sea on the west, the Kallai river on the south, Vellayil village on the north, and Kozhikode town on the east
facts.source_title: Kuttichira Beach

facts.fact: The beach runs roughly from Beypore in the south to Kappad in the north, covering South Beach, Vellayil, and Kallayi sections of Kozhikode city's coastline.
facts.quote: The beach extends from Beypore (south) to Kappad (north)
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach

facts.fact: The beach is reached from the city via four separate road overbridges.
facts.quote: The beach is accessible through four road overbridges in the city.
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach

facts.fact: The Kozhikode district government's own tourism page states Calicut International Airport is about 29 km from the beach and the railway station about 3 km away — a road/route figure, not the straight-line 24.4 km in this beach's dataset.
facts.quote: Air: Kozhikode International Airport is approximately 29 km away... Rail: Kozhikode railway station located about 3 km away
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach | Kozhikode District Website

facts.fact: Vellayil, the beach segment on the city's northern side, sits at 11°16'21"N 75°45'56"E and connects south to Kozhikode via Gandhi Road toward Nadakkavu.
facts.quote: Vellayil is a beach on the northern side of Kozhikode city.
facts.source_title: Vellayil

facts.fact: After Mahatma Gandhi's 1934 visit to Kozhikode, the beachfront Beach Road (previously called Evan's Road) was renamed Gandhi Road.
facts.quote: the beach road was renamed 'Gandhi Road'
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach

facts.fact: In April 1950, land on Kozhikode beach was acquired to build a Government Headquarters hospital.
facts.quote: In April 1950, land was acquired on the Kozhikode beach to build a Government Headquarters hospital.
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach

facts.fact: The northern 'Iron Screw-pile' pier was built in 1871, running 400 ft (120 m) out to sea with a T-shaped end; it and a second pier once carried cranes for loading spices onto trading ships and now stand deteriorated.
facts.quote: The 'Iron Screw-pile' pier to the north was built in 1871, 400 ft long (120 m) with a 'T' end.
facts.source_title: List of tourist attractions in Kozhikode

facts.fact: Kozhikode's lighthouse began in 1847 as a 33 m stone tower with a coconut-oil wick lamp; it was rebuilt at 15 m in 1903 with the new light activated in 1907, converted to acetylene flashing in 1924, and converted again to a solar-powered LED flashing light in 2008 — it is now an automated, largely defunct aid.
facts.quote: converted to LED flashing light using solar energy in 2008
facts.source_title: Kozhikkode Lighthouse

facts.fact: The beach was a major independence-era rally ground, hosting speeches by Mahatma Gandhi, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, Indira Gandhi, and V.K. Krishna Menon.
facts.quote: hosted major rallies where national leaders including Mahatma Gandhi, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, Indira Gandhi, and Krishna Menon delivered speeches
facts.source_title: List of tourist attractions in Kozhikode

facts.fact: The 15th-century Sanskrit travel-poem Kokila Sandesa by the poet Uddanda describes Kozhikode's coast (as 'Kukkatakroda') being showered with 'a shipful of jewels,' an early literary record of the shore as a trading harbor.
facts.quote: seeing that his daughter [goddess of riches] has settled down in Kukkatakroda [Kozhikode], is embracing the place, presenting it with a shipful of jewels
facts.source_title: List of tourist attractions in Kozhikode

facts.fact: Kerala Tourism's promotional copy for Kozhikode Beach credits 'this coastline' with Vasco da Gama's 1498 arrival, but the documented landing (a plaque dates it to May 27, 1498) was at Kappad Beach, 16 km north of Kozhikode town.
facts.quote: 16 km distance from Kozhikode town to Kappad is corroborated across multiple independent travel sources; the Kappad Wikipedia article does not state this figure.
facts.source_title: Kappad (landing site); 16 km distance is corroborated but not Wikipedia-sourced

facts.fact: Kappad Beach (with Chal Beach in Kannur) received Blue Flag certification from the Denmark-based Foundation for Environmental Education in February 2025; Kozhikode Beach itself holds no Blue Flag certification.
facts.quote: This honour reflects Kerala's ongoing dedication to environmental conservation and sustainable tourism.
facts.source_title: Kappad and Chal Beaches Blue Flag Certified

facts.fact: A 2016-17 municipal beautification project spent Rs 3.85 crore on an 800 m by 10 m stretch south of the wharf, centered on a 330-metre sea-facing walkway with four viewpoints and shelters; District Collector U.V. Jose called it the project's centerpiece.
facts.quote: The focal point is the 330-meter walkway annexed to the sea.
facts.source_title: Kozhikode beach beautification in progress

facts.fact: A parallel Rs 4 crore renovation — an open stage, repaired sea-facing notches, lighting and toilets, and relocation of the beach's handcart vendors — was budgeted but had not yet started as of the December 2017 report, with work expected to begin within about 45 days.
facts.quote: Rs 4 crore is allotted for the renovation of Kozhikode beach with an open stage, repairing the broken down notches, installation of lights and toilets
facts.source_title: Kozhikode beach beautification in progress

facts.fact: As of the December 2017 Deccan Chronicle report, the Rs 3.85-crore promenade beautification project's first phase was still in progress, expected to finish by early March 2018 — not yet complete at the time of reporting.
facts.quote: The beautification work of south beach started in June last year is progressing... expected to finish by early March
facts.source_title: Kozhikode beach beautification in progress

facts.fact: On the night of October 15-16, 2025, the sea receded roughly 200 metres along a 1.5 km stretch of South Beach in a 'rare phenomenon,' then the effect shifted the next morning to the stretch opposite the Corporation office; CMFRI scientists and the taluk tahsildar inspected the site.
facts.quote: There was a high tide in the morning, which returned to normal by 8 am.
facts.source_title: Water recedes at Kozhikode beach in rare phenomenon

facts.fact: A local ward councillor described the exposed seabed as calm and wave-free overnight during the October 2025 event, but said the sea turned rougher and the water muddier by morning — an account that sits uneasily next to officials' tidal explanation.
facts.quote: the exposed area remained calm without waves overnight; conditions changed by morning with rougher seas and muddy-appearing water
facts.source_title: Water recedes at Kozhikode beach in rare phenomenon

facts.fact: The October 2025 recession was not unprecedented: in October 2022 the sea similarly receded about 50 metres at Kothi Beach near Nainamvalappu, elsewhere in Kozhikode, with a tsunami officially ruled out at the time.
facts.quote: the sea receded up to 50 metres at the Kothi Beach near Nainamvalappu in Kozhikode
facts.source_title: Sea recedes about 50 metres in Kozhikode, Tsunami ruled out

facts.fact: Kozhikode district's 78 km coastline carries 53 km of seawalls and 16 groins, but an August 2022 field survey found only about 10.5 km of seawall still intact, 28.1 km partly damaged, and 14.4 km in poor or collapsed condition.
facts.quote: Only about 10.5 km of seawalls remain intact... 28.1 km are partly damaged... 14.4 km are in poor or collapsed condition.
facts.source_title: Mapping Kerala's Coastal Defences: From Field Survey to Shoreline Management Plans

facts.fact: The same coastal survey found 10-25 m of beach still standing near Kozhikode Beach, Vellayil, Puthiyappa, and Kappad, while the beach had vanished entirely at Kadduka bazar, Vakkadavu, Bhatt Road, and Thuvvapara elsewhere in the district.
facts.quote: 10-25 m wide beaches... near Godhishawaram, Kozhikode beach, Vellayil, Puthiyappa, and Kappad
facts.source_title: Mapping Kerala's Coastal Defences: From Field Survey to Shoreline Management Plans

facts.fact: In the same district, four people (including two women) drowned after being swept by strong waves off Thikkodi beach — about 25 km north of Kozhikode Beach, a distinct location — on January 27, 2025; local people and fishermen carried out the rescue rather than official lifeguards.
facts.quote: Four persons including two women drowned after they were swept away by strong waves off Thikkodi beach in Kozhikode.
facts.source_title: Kerala: 4 drown in strong waves off Thikkodi beach

facts.fact: Kozhikode district was among Kerala's worst-hit by Cyclone Ockhi in late November-December 2017, the most intense Arabian Sea cyclone since Cyclone Megh (2015).
facts.quote: The worst affected districts include Ernakulam, Kollam, Alappuzha, Kozhikode, and Kasargod.
facts.source_title: Cyclone Ockhi

facts.fact: The Malabar Mahotsavam, an annual cultural festival held every January at Kozhikode Beach and organized by Kerala's Department of Tourism, features Theyyam, Kathakali, and Kalaripayattu performances alongside music, handicrafts, and a food festival.
facts.quote: This colorful cultural extravaganza in January showcases the art, culture and cuisine of Malabar
facts.source_title: Malabar Mahotsavam Festival in Calicut

facts.fact: On August 9, 2026, Kerala's public-distribution agency Supplyco opened a Mega Trade Fair at Kozhikode Beach — a 4,000-sq-ft air-conditioned 'German Hangar' structure running 10 am-9 pm through August 25 — inaugurated by Minister P.K. Kunhalikutty and selling discounted Onam kits, including a Rs 2,000, 30-item 'Thiruvonam Kit' at a Rs 540 discount.
facts.quote: The market intervention by Supplyco makes necessities accessible to ordinary citizens during expensive festival seasons
facts.source_title: Supplyco Onam Mega Trade Fair starts at Kozhikode Beach

facts.fact: Kozhikode Municipal Corporation, which administers the city (118.58 sq km, about 609,224 people) across 76 wards, is the civic body whose jurisdiction covers the beach, though no ward-specific beach authority is separately documented.
facts.quote: 118.58 km² of the city of Kozhikode, with a population of about 609,224
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Municipal Corporation

facts.fact: SM Street ('Sweet Meat Street,' Malayalam: Mittai Theruvu), a 2.1 km market street dating to the era of Zamorin rule, got its English name because its signature dark-red ghee halwa looked to British visitors like a cut of meat.
facts.quote: the classic red ghee halwa looked like a cut of meat, prompting the British to name the street 'Sweet Meat Street'
facts.source_title: Memories of a sweet street: Kozhikode 'Mittai Theruvu' has been around for centuries

facts.fact: Kozhikkodan Halwa traces to Arab spice traders and, by legend, was first gifted to the Zamorin of Kozhikode; it is made from maida flour, sugar or jaggery, ghee, and nuts, and takes about two hours to prepare.
facts.quote: the Kozhikkodan Halwa takes about two hours to prepare
facts.source_title: Kozhikkodan Halwa | Sweet Street Kozhikode

facts.fact: Along the beach promenade itself, stalls sell kallummakaya (fried/breaded mussels), banana chips, quail eggs, and ice cream rather than sit-down restaurant fare.
facts.quote: Kallummakkaya (mussels fry), banana chips, ice-cream, and the iconic Calicut halwa
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach in Kozhikode | Districts of Malabar, Kerala

facts.fact: The beach includes a children's play area, 'Lions Park,' and an adjacent aquarium, alongside paved-stone walkways and evening illumination.
facts.quote: The beach has paved stones and illumination, and there is one Lions Park for the children and an aquarium.
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach

facts.fact: Kerala Tourism promotes 'Dolphin's Point' along the beach as a spot for early-morning dolphin sightings — a tourism-board claim with no independent marine survey found to confirm it.
facts.quote: Early risers can head to Dolphin's Point to catch glimpses of dolphins frolicking in the sea
facts.source_title: Kozhikode Beach | Calicut Beach | Kerala Coastal Attractions

facts.fact: India's ocean-information agency INCOIS had separately flagged rough-sea and 'black sea phenomenon' alerts for the coast between Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam around the same period as the October 2025 Kozhikode event — a different stretch of Kerala's coastline, underscoring that Kozhikode's event was not covered by a regional advisory.
facts.quote: issued alerts about potential 'black sea phenomenon' and rough seas from Thiruvananthapuram to Kollam
facts.source_title: Water recedes at Kozhikode beach in rare phenomenon

facts.fact: The Malayalam Wikipedia article on this beach independently corroborates it as the city's primary venue for public meetings, matching the English-language record of 20th-century political rallies here.
facts.quote: പൊതുയോഗങ്ങള്‍ നടത്തുന്നതിനുള്ള പ്രധാന സ്ഥലമാണ് കോഴിക്കോട് ബീച്ച്
facts.source_title: കോഴിക്കോട് കടപ്പുറം (Malayalam Wikipedia)

recency.newest_item: August 9, 2026 — Kerala's Supplyco opened a Mega Trade Fair at Kozhikode Beach (running through August 25, 2026), inaugurated by Minister P.K. Kunhalikutty (Manorama Online).

dead_ends: No official or press source confirms lifeguard staffing, designated swimming zones, or beach-closure protocols specifically at Kozhikode Beach itself (distinct from other district beaches where fatalities were reported).
No currently-operating named restaurant, hotel, or business at or near the beach was found with its own website or dated press coverage confirming it — businesses list is empty by design.
No official municipal or tourism-board fee schedule for beach entry or parking was located; multiple third-party travel blogs claim free entry, but none is an official source.
No film, TV show, song, or book was found that names Kozhikode Beach itself as a location (only a general, unrelated count of ~167 films shot somewhere in Kozhikode city).
No official source states whether the 29 km airport figure (kozhikode.nic.in) is a road distance or an approximation; no press-confirmed taxi fare or drive time to the beach was found.
No official water-quality testing or lifeguard-count data for Kozhikode Beach was found, despite an extensive search of Kerala coastal-safety reporting.
conflicts: Kerala Tourism's Kozhikode Beach page (F01/F13 source) implies the Vasco da Gama 1498 landing happened on 'this coastline,' while Wikipedia and Kerala Tourism's own Kappad Beach page place the documented landing 16 km north at Kappad Beach (F13).

kozhikode.nic.in states Calicut International Airport is 'approximately 29 km' from the beach (F05); this beach's own dataset (site/data/beaches/kozhikode-beach.json) records nearest_airport.distance_km as 24.4, explicitly as a straight-line figure — neither source confirms an actual road distance.

CMFRI's quoted tidal explanation for the October 2025 water recession (F17) does not fully square with the ward councillor's account of anomalously calm, wave-free water overnight (F18); officials offered a routine explanation for what residents described as unusual.
